instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Take the Consequence
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility for carrying out the cost, penalty, or unpleasant next step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You lost the chess game. The agreement says you wash up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we were joking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. You were very serious about my washing up while you were winning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we play again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the dishes. Call it a practical interval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plan cost more. You agreed to announce the budget cut; bring me your opening sentence before the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only cost slightly more. Can't we skip the announcement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. You may keep the announcement short. Name the cut and the reason, and I'll check the figures.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could explain it better. Will you do the talking if I stand beside you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll check your explanation with you beforehand. At the meeting you speak; I'll stand beside you and hold the figures. You can point to them while you explain why the cut is needed.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I accept your verdict on my picnic, tell me how you're measuring success. I'll hear the criteria first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone having fun. It looked successful to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me what a successful picnic gets you, and where my organizing ranks against last year's. We'll put those beside 'fun.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I get the activities budget renewed. Yours cost less, but last year's attracted more people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You may score cost and attendance separately. Now tell me which one decides my ranking when you ask for that renewal; I want to know what my success is being used to prove.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you call your cousin the better club-president candidate, tell me what you gain if he beats me. I'll hear your measure of 'better.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A competent president. Isn't that enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As a heading. Which of your proposals gets easier, and where does that put me in your ranking?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He supports my car-park resurfacing plan. You want the money spent on the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put both projects under the heading. You may prefer his, but tell me whether you're ranking our competence or your chance of getting the car park. I'll take the comparison in those terms.

cards.title: Enter on My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit them into your side of a contest or bargain before the stakes become fully clear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Put on our quiz-team badge before I explain the final round.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why? What happens if we lose?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We'll face that together. That's what the badge means.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to face anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's start with the very easy agreement to wear blue.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Raise the Stakes
cards.instruction: Persuade them to accept a larger risk, cost, or commitment so the outcome will feel decisive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll play this chess game for a proper stake: the loser cooks all weekend. You can make the first move once we agree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were playing for a biscuit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it beside the board as a reminder of how little we used to risk. This result should decide more than who gets a snack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I work both days this weekend. I couldn't cook even if I lost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll allow weeknights instead. Five dinners, whoever loses. We'll remember every move while eating them. Accept that and open; I'll put my whole menu at risk too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll accept a rematch with real terms: your captaincy against my place on the team. Put both beside the score before we start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a ridiculous risk. One bad game could change everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You may call it a bad game afterward, but we'll both know which result changed the team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Isn't pride enough? We could just announce the winner at dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Announce the terms at dinner instead; we'll play tomorrow. We've forgotten six games played for pride. Let everyone hear which role each of us is risking before we compete. Tomorrow's announcement will have something to settle.

cards.title: Name My Contribution
cards.instruction: Get them to acknowledge exactly what your effort, sacrifice, or strategy added to the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring me the festival thank-you speech before you read it. I want the stage repair in the rain named properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll thank everyone equally. They all helped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may give us equal time. Use my sentence to say what the repair made possible, not just that I got wet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So you want your name in the speech?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside the fact that the dancers had a stage to stand on. Read that line back to me, then give everyone else their contribution as clearly. I'll hear mine in the same terms.
